correctness.rationale: Exact normalized Funk-Hecke formula gives a two-column matrix in every spherical-harmonic degree. For 0<u<v<j_{nu,1}/b all matrix entries are positive. DLMF product and ordered zeros give a strictly positive log derivative of the ratio of the two columns, making the determinant negative. L1 harmonic completeness establishes injectivity; one trace has a nontrivial harmonic nullspace. Bessel power-series expansion through its first 1/(ell+nu+1) correction gives the sharp negative determinant, and singular-value product and dominant entry give both asymptotics. Actual independent numerical tests verify constants and normalization but are not used as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: A 2011 full-text theorem and 2020 full-text generalization each have only one independent source sphere. The proposed Fourier recovery uses two independent source densities, a sign-definite 2-by-2 Bessel minor across two measurement radii, and sharp large-degree singular-value asymptotics. Standard Bessel identities are credited as ingredients; a full covering theorem was not found in the actual comparisons. Older literature is a recorded publication-priority risk.

value.rationale: A natural two-shell inverse-source problem requires determining the exact number of complete frequency traces and whether recovery is numerically stable. The result supplies the sharp minimum of two, an explicit all-dimensional frequency region, a strict mode-by-mode sign invariant, and a sharp factorial high-angular-degree small-singular-value law. This quantitative instability is necessary information for assessing any regularization and is not a routine isolated parameter evaluation.
